verdict.reasoning: Patient reports diarrhea for three days and describes it as initially watery then very loose: 'It was three days ago' and 'it's very loose but it started as being very watery.'
Patient says they have lost count of bowel movements and notes 'Today alone, I've been at least four time,' supporting more than four today and overall loss of count.

Patient states: 'I've been throwing up. I can't seem to be able to keep anything in me. Not even water, not even my tea, not even any liquid stuff. I've just been throwing up everything' and 'I was sick ... maybe about two hours ago,' supporting vomiting after intake and inability to keep fluids down with last episode ~2 hours ago.

Patient reports feeling very hot but no thermometer used: 'Yes, I've been running a serious temperature. I'm literally boiling' and 'No, 'cause I've not got one but like, to the touch, I'm, like, literally roasting.'

Pain location and relation to urge are described: 'it's kind of like towards my navel area... almost like the center of my navel' and 'When it comes, I feel this strong urge to go to the loo,' supporting intermittent peri-umbilical pain preceding defecation; describing it as crampy is a reasonable clinical inference from context.
Doctor asks about blood and patient replies: 'And any blood in the stool or in the urine that you've noticed?' / 'No blood.'
Urination details: 'Yeah, I've been, yeah, urinating OK' and 'Um. an hour ago' for last urine; color: 'To be honest, I have a look so I really couldn't say,' indicating she did not check color.
No travel and brother ill: 'Have you been abroad anywhere?' / 'No,' and 'my brother ... has actually been having similar symptoms ... and he does say like everyone in school's got this.'
Baseline bowel habit: 'my bowels is normally fine. I would normally go to the toilet every day. You know, in the morning, just once' and 'Any episodes of diarrhoea or constipation normally?' / 'No.'

Patient mentions menstrual cramps but no statement that overall past medical history is otherwise unremarkable: 'Obviously I get the odd, um, you know, menstrual cramps' without a global PMH review. Labeling PMH as unremarkable except dysmenorrhea adds information not explicitly confirmed.
Occupation, work status, and household are stated: 'A graphics designer,' 'I'm working from home today because I can't, I can't be out for work,' and 'I live with my brother and my mum.'
Substance use: 'Well, I don't smoke, but, you know, I have a pint from time to time' and 'And do you take any other drugs?' / 'No. Like I said, I only take, um, vitamins.'
Medication history: 'I take my, my vitamins, vitamin D, every day. That's about all that I regularly take' and 'for my menstrual cramps ... I might take a, a, an ibuprofen just to ease the pain.'

Doctor’s assessment: 'it sounds like it might be some, an infectious gastroenteritis that you've got, which is usually caused by a virus. But, it can be from something you've eaten, as well.' This supports acute infectious gastroenteritis, likely viral.

Risk of dehydration is explicitly discussed: 'the key thing is that we want to make sure that you're hydrated enough' and 'we should also check that you're not getting dehydrated, because if you're, if you're not keeping fluid down, then you can get dehydrated.'

'I think it's probably important to get a sample of the stool, so we can make sure that you haven't got a nasty bacterial infection' and 'we should see you so that we can check your hydration and, um, get that sample sent off as soon as possible... we can make you an urgent appointment,' which implies stool testing (MCS) and urgent clinic visit.
ORS instructions: 'you need to carry on with your rehydration salts, and just have very small amounts' and later 'Just tiny sips constantly, to so that your stomach doesn't get overfilled.'

Diet advice: 'just have very simple food, if you're gonna have anything, like toast or biscuit or something really light like that. Avoid, um, fruit, vegetables, uh, milk, anything like that, which might just make it worse.'

Escalation for worsening/poor hydration: 'if, in the meantime, you're feeling more unwell, then we would get you seen urgently in A and E' and focus on hydration; while urine monitoring is not literally stated, the plan centers on hydration and escalation if unable to hydrate, supporting the overall content with minor inferred phrasing.

Follow-up and booking: 'So you'll have to book an appointment through the support line' and 'So you can call us back in the meantime,' matching booking via support line and calling if symptoms escalate.
